title: Toward Appraisal-Structured Latent Control Representations in Language Models: A Preregistered Hypothesis and Experimental Design for Task-Induced Response-Strategy Modulation
description: A preregistered hypothesis and experimental-design note proposing that several known single-behavior latent directions in language models may be special cases of a more general family of task-induced, appraisal-structured latent control representations. Version 0.1.2 is a pre-data methodological correction: it replaces a non-identifying H1 decision statistic with bidirectional cross-mention leave-one-domain-out transfer, separates H1 from H2, fixes training-only selection, strengthens axis-isolation QA, defines Layer-0 pooling, and separates technical smoke logs from scientific feasibility artifacts. Later pre-data review binds the H2 target, estimand, independent comparator selection, estimability and response-label reliability; freezes the probe pipeline, regularization grid, tie-breaking and seed roles; replaces mixed-domain inner folds with inner leave-one-training-domain-out; specifies the cluster bootstrap and Benjamini-Hochberg raw-p procedures; requires a compatible frozen config, run plan, manifest and canonical stimulus hash before Mini-0; separates the later H3 gate; and fixes one canonical deterministic document build. No data have been collected, no model has been run, and no results exist.
